subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards support an opt-in append/delta payload mode, or should OpenClaw keep full-content CardKit updates only and solve long-reply latency another way?
rationale: Current main follows the full-content behavior that fixed truncation, but the latest live repro says the coalescing candidate did not fix the latency; choosing a new mode or rejecting it changes a user-facing plugin contract and possibly config surface.

options.title: Design A Safe Opt-In Mode
options.body: Add a narrowly documented append/delta transport mode only after live Feishu proof shows it fixes latency without truncating final content in the affected tenant shape.

options.title: Repair And Prove The Coalescing PR
options.body: Keep full-content semantics and require the linked PR to provide exact-head live Feishu proof that a cadence-only change fixes long-reply latency before merge.

options.title: Reject Append Mode For Now
options.body: Keep full-content updates as the only streaming contract and document `streaming: false` or `renderMode: "raw"` as the supported workaround for slow tenants.

recommendation.title: Design A Safe Opt-In Mode
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly documented append/delta transport mode only after live Feishu proof shows it fixes latency without truncating final content in the affected tenant shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the community maintainer for @openclaw/feishu, and this decision is Feishu plugin behavior rather than core runtime policy.
